newsitem.title: INDIA: Hindu lawmakers disrupt Indian parliament again.
newsitem.headline: Hindu lawmakers disrupt Indian parliament again.

text.p: Protesting right-wing Hindu lawmakers paralysed India's parliament on Friday, forcing the abrupt adjournment of both houses for the third consecutive day.

The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) led the charge, raising slogans against the governor of the most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, where the party claims it has been denied a chance to rule.
"Sack Bhandari!" BJP lawmakers shouted from the well of the lower house, or Lok Sabha, denouncing Uttar Pradesh governor Ramesh Bhandari.
The BJP was joined by its regional allies in Maharashtra state, the Shiv Sena party, who demanded that two districts in neighbouring Karnataka state, Belgaum and Karwar, be folded into Maharashtra.
"We'll take Belgaum and Karwar!" Shiv Sena lawmakers yelled.
The Lok Sabha speaker, unable to quell the din, quickly adjourned the house and ordered all official business put off until next week.
"It is a shame for the nation," speaker P.A. Sangma said. "You should be ashamed. If the members of parliament behave like this, it is a shameful thing."

The upper house, or Rajya Sabha, also adjourned amid loud shouting by BJP members. They were joined by members from the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, who demanded immediate debate over a recent cyclone which killed 971 people people and left 925 missing.
Both houses were expected to resume official business on Tuesday. Monday is a religious holiday.
"I hope a long adjournment will calm down the people and the house can function," Vice President Kocheril Raman Narayanan, who heads the upper house, said.

Last December, BJP deputies virtually paralysed business during the month-long winter session of parliament. They were protesting the government's telephone privatisation programme and alleged irregularities by government officials.

Former communications minister Sukh Ram, who served under then prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and spearheaded the privatisation programme, has since been arrested and charged with bribery. Sukh Ram says he is innocent.
BJP deputies privately said they expected the din over Uttar Pradesh, which dominated attention during the first three days of this winter session of parliament, to die down next week.
The BJP emerged as the biggest single party in recent assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh but fell short of an outright majority.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front coalition came in second, and the Congress party, allied with a regional party representing the lowest Hindu castes, came in third.
No political grouping was able to muster the necessary majority to form a state government.
Claiming a political impasse, President Shankar Dayal Sharma last month accepted a recommendation by governor Bhandari and imposed federal rule over the state, home to some 140 million people.
